I always heard how good this game was, that it was the gold standard for roguelikes and everything about it was top notch. After finally deciding to try it and enjoying it so much to the point I got all the achievements, I can without a doubt say that it lived up to the hype and then some.

Its not very often I play a game where the banter and dialog gets me invested but I found myself not really skipping or speeding up through the chatting and looked forward to seeing what new dialog options popped up after each new run. All the characters have distinct personalities and the voice actors did a phenomenal job in each role, not a weak link among them.

All in all it was a blast and after beating this game I immediately started on Hades II, and man would you believe that it gets even better?

Upon writing this review, I've almost clocked in 72 hours hours in this game, I've completed the main story, and I'm still working towards 100% completion. And honestly? I'm still not tired of it.

I love everything about this game. The dialogues, the story progression, the character development, the way every character feels like an actual person with their own personality and history. The way the story unfolds naturally as you keep playing, even when you're dying over and over again, is just brilliant. You don't feel like you're grinding through the same content. You feel like you're slowly becoming part of this world.

And then there's the gameplay.

Every run feels like its own little adventure. The randomness keeps things fresh, and the weapons are so incredibly unique that switching between them genuinely changes the way you approach a run. The different weapon aspects add even more variety, and the sheer number of boons you can acquire and combine to create some absolutely ridiculous builds is just *chef's kiss*. There's something incredibly satisfying about finding a combination that works perfectly and watching everything fall into place.

But what I appreciate the most is how seamlessly everything comes together. The gameplay, the writing, the progression, the characters, the music, the art style. Nothing feels like it's there just to fill space. Even failure feels like progress, and that's something I absolutely adore about this game.

While I have finished the main story, I still have things left to discover, builds to experiment with, and reasons to keep coming back. And that's probably the biggest compliment I can give a game like this.

I guess I would recommend this game but I'm personally very mixed on it.

While the art, world building, voice acting and characters are all great, I find the story and gameplay to be lackluster. Especially for a rogue lite. It lacks variety, so runs become stale pretty quickly, and while most rogue likes could be beaten on your first run with a lot of luck, Hades is not designed to be beaten on your first run.

The story is praised a lot, too, but from what I've seen it's pretty barebones. There's some world-building and lore you can find, but the main plot is pretty boring. I found myself skipping through dialogue in the lobby because it took too long and only 10% of the time was there new information.

I find the game to be a bit clunkily executed, especially if you're a rogue-like veteran. So my judgment is this: If you love rogue likes, don't bother with this one, it'll lack variety for you and become stale quickly. But if you want to get into rogue likes then this is the perfect entry point for you, and probably why this game entered the mainstream in the first place.

(This review contains minor mechanical spoilers, and mentions minor details about the sequel at the end)

Hades is one of the few games I always enjoy returning to, even after having completed the full story several times. The incredible attention to detail and unique style present in every aspect of the game have always impressed me, from the first time I played.

The story is extremely well-written, immersive, and impactful. I was hooked to it and eager to progress it all the way through, and have started up a new save file to experience it again several times over the years. Progress feels meaningful and personal. More than any other game I have played, the world feels developed and alive. Characters have depth and respond to the things the player does, sometimes in the funniest and most unexpected ways. After over 200 hours of gameplay, I still encounter dialogues I haven't seen before.

I greatly enjoy the combat system. It's simple but also has a high ceiling to develop your skill, and there is lots of room for personal preference. There are many mechanics which exist to provide variety to the builds you can make and incentives for exploring that variety, but also freedom to play the way you want to. There is room to choose how difficult you want the game to be— whether more casual to experience the story, or more challenging to push your limits. Players who enjoy challenges can utilize some optional mechanics that increase the difficulty in creative ways which push you to make use of everything you can, and be rewarded for doing so. Unlike many games, it's not just artificial difficulty either, there is genuinely unique content to enjoy in doing so (i.e. not just numbers going up, which is part of it, but also interesting twists and enemies gaining new attacks & abilities).

There is also SO much content and replayability. Outside of the main story, there are so many other things you can choose to explore and progress, including side storylines, customizations, challenges, additional worldbuilding, and more. It doesn't feel like a chore, either— you can work on many things at once by just playing the game. Completionists can have a field day trying to max everything out if they so please. And, since the dungeons are randomized and there are so many build choices, no two runs feel the same. You are compelled to improve your adaptability and be ready for anything. At the same time, I would say the RNG is well-balanced, and there are systems you can unlock to greatly mitigate build-based RNG once you start finding ones you like to go for.

Overall, I would say Hades deserves all the awards and nominations it's received and more, and I can easily recommend it to a variety of players. You can tell the developers put the utmost of their efforts and passion into making it. I love the art style and original music so much I've used screenshots as my desktop background and listen to the music outside of the game. With Hades 2 out now, there's even more to look forward to afterwards. I would highly recommend playing the original first, as while Hades 2 has its own story, it builds on the story from the first game and has lots of fun references.
